q-35796.name: Question 1
q-35796.worked_solution:
We substitute $t=-2$ into the function definition and then simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(t) & =(t+1)^{2}-2(t+1) \\ f(-2) & =(-2+1)^{2}-2(-2+1) \\  & =(-1)^{2}-2(-1) \\  & =1+2 \\  & =3\end{aligned}
$$

Find the value of f(t)=(t+1)2−2(t+1) at t=−2.

a
0
b
−8
c
−1
d
3
e
6
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We substitute t=−2 into the function definition and then simplify:

f(t)=(t+1)2−2(t+1)f(−2)=(−2+1)2−2(−2+1)=(−1)2−2(−1)=1+2=3

q-130589.name: Question 3
q-130589.worked_solution:
We substitute $x=-3$ and $y=0$ into the function definition and then simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y) & ={5}^{x+4}+x\cdot {2}^{y+1} \\ f(-3,0) & ={5}^{-3+4}+(-3)\cdot {2}^{0+1} \\  & ={5}^{1}+(-3)\cdot {2}^{1} \\  & ={5}^{1}-3\cdot 2 \\  & =5-6 \\  & =-1\end{aligned}
$$

q-214851.name: Question 4
q-214851.worked_solution:
We substitute $u=5$ and $v=3$ into the function definition and then simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}g(u,v) & =3\cdot {5}^{2u-3v}-2u \\ g(5,3) & =3\cdot {5}^{2(5)-3(3)}-2(5) \\  & =3\cdot {5}^{10-9}-10 \\  & =3\cdot {5}^{1}-10 \\  & =15-10 \\  & =5\end{aligned}
$$
